questions.q: Which pump is used to move water vertically from an underground cistern to an overhead tank?
questions.n: Transfer pumps are specifically designed for the vertical movement of water between storage containers.

questions.q: Which pump is connected to a fire sprinkler system to maintain pressure in the sprinkler pipes?
questions.n: Jockey pumps compensate for small pressure drops to prevent the main fire pump from cycling unnecessarily.

questions.q: Which fire suppression system is commonly used in parking garages?
questions.n: Dry pipe systems prevent water from freezing in the pipes, making them ideal for unheated spaces.

questions.q: What is the term for the network of pipes that supplies water vertically to the sprinkler system in a multi-story building?
questions.n: The riser is the vertical backbone of the piping system that carries water to the various levels of a structure.

questions.q: Which type of smoke detector is best suited for detecting fast-flaming fires?
questions.n: Ionization detectors are highly sensitive to the small particles produced by fast-flaming fires.

questions.q: Which fire extinguisher class is required for fires involving energized electrical equipment?
questions.n: Class C extinguishers use non-conductive agents suitable for fires involving live electrical components.

questions.q: What is the standard acronym used to remember how to operate a fire extinguisher?
questions.n: P.A.S.S. stands for Pull, Aim, Squeeze, and Sweep, describing the correct sequence of actions.

questions.q: What type of detector is most appropriate for a kitchen or garage where smoke and steam are common?
questions.n: Heat detectors avoid false alarms from smoke or steam, making them ideal for kitchens and garages.

questions.q: Which fire extinguisher type is mandatory for commercial kitchens involving vegetable oils and animal fats?
questions.n: Class K extinguishers use a wet chemical agent that turns fats into soap through saponification.

questions.q: At what stage of a fire should a portable fire extinguisher be used?
questions.n: The incipient stage is the very beginning of a small, contained fire where extinguishers are most effective.

questions.q: Which section of RA 9266 is titled 'Structural Design, Building Materials, and Architectural Specifications, and Methods of Construction and Utilities'?
questions.n: As per the Supreme Court E-Library, this section specifically covers the technical aspects of the architecture board exam.

questions.q: In a fire sprinkler system, what is the primary function of a Siamesed Connection?
o: To regulate the pressure of the jockey pump
To sense the flow of water and trigger the alarm
To drain the system during maintenance
To allow the fire department to pump additional water and pressure into the system
questions.n: This exterior connection acts as an intake for fire trucks to supplement the building's water supply.

questions.q: What is the standard minimum clearance between the top of storage and a sprinkler deflector?
questions.n: This vertical gap is required to allow the water spray pattern to develop fully without obstruction.

questions.q: Which fire suppression system contains pressurized nitrogen or air to prevent water from entering the pipes until a head is activated?
questions.n: Dry pipe systems are specifically designed for unheated areas to prevent water from freezing inside the pipes.

questions.q: Which type of detector is best for detecting smoldering fires using a light beam and sensor?
questions.n: These detectors rely on light scattering, making them highly effective for the larger particles found in smoldering fires.

questions.q: What type of building is classified as a 'light hazard' for fire protection purposes?
questions.n: Residential spaces have lower fuel loads compared to commercial or industrial settings.

questions.q: A Class K fire extinguisher is mandatory for which of the following environments?
questions.n: Class K is designed for high-temperature vegetable oils and animal fats used in professional cooking.

questions.q: Which sprinkler head is designed to be installed pointing upward toward the ceiling?
questions.n: Upright heads are installed on top of piping to spray water against a deflector that directs it downward.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the minimum PSI for a Class A concrete mixture?
questions.n: As per updated ALE technical standards, Class A concrete is rated at 3500 PSI.

questions.q: What device manually triggers a fire alarm system when pulled by a person?
questions.n: This is the initiating device designed for human interaction during an emergency.

questions.q: Which pump is designed to increase water pressure when the existing municipal supply is inadequate?
questions.n: Booster pumps 'boost' the pressure of an incoming line to meet the building's demand.

questions.q: In an addressable fire alarm system, what is the primary advantage over conventional systems?
o: It is cheaper to install in small buildings
Each device has a unique ID for exact location identification
questions.n: Addressable systems pinpoint the specific room or detector that was triggered.

questions.q: What is the maximum travel distance to a Class A fire extinguisher in most buildings?
questions.n: This standard ensures that an extinguisher is accessible within a reasonable walking distance.

questions.q: Which fire suppression system is recommended for museums where water damage to artifacts must be avoided?
questions.n: Pre-action systems require two separate triggers, greatly reducing the risk of accidental discharge.

questions.q: What color is the label typically associated with a Class K fire extinguisher?
questions.n: Though the canister is often silver, the identifying label for Class K (Kitchen) is black.

questions.q: Which pump uses a rotating impeller to move water and create pressure via centrifugal force?
questions.n: This is the most common pump type in building utilities, using velocity to create pressure.

questions.q: Which standpipe class is intended for use specifically by firefighters during a fire?
questions.n: Class I systems provide 2.5-inch hose connections designed for heavy-duty firefighting equipment.

questions.q: In BP 344, what is the required minimum width of a corridor for accessibility?
questions.n: This width allows for the comfortable passage of a wheelchair and the possibility of another person passing.

questions.q: Which fire suppression system is most suitable for protecting electrical transformers or tanks with flammable liquids?
questions.n: Mist systems use high pressure to create fine droplets that cool the fire and displace oxygen without flooding.

questions.q: What is the secondary power source required for all fire alarm systems?
questions.n: Fire codes require a dedicated battery backup to ensure the system works during a power outage.

questions.q: Which detector is best for high-ceiling warehouses using a projected beam of light?
questions.n: Beam detectors cover large open areas where individual point detectors would be difficult to install.

questions.q: What is the primary use of a Class D fire extinguisher?
questions.n: Class D agents (like sodium chloride) are specifically for metals like magnesium or titanium.

questions.q: Why should you never use a water extinguisher on a grease fire?
o: Water provides more fuel to the fire
Water causes the flaming oil to splash and spread the fire rapidly
Water makes the smoke more toxic
Water is too expensive for grease fires
questions.n: Water is denser than oil and turns to steam instantly, causing an explosive expansion of burning grease.

questions.q: Which pump is typically installed beneath an elevator pit for drainage?
questions.n: Sump pumps are designed to clear water that accumulates in low-lying pits or basements.

questions.q: Which component of a fire sprinkler head melts at a specific temperature to release water?
questions.n: This can be a glass bulb or a fusible link that breaks/melts to activate the sprinkler.

questions.q: What does the 'ABC' label on a multi-purpose dry chemical extinguisher signify?
o: The sequence of steps: Aim, Blow, Control
Effective against ordinary combustibles, flammable liquids, and electrical fires
questions.n: The label indicates the extinguisher is safe and effective for multiple types of hazards.

questions.q: Which fire suppression system is considered the most reliable and most common for general buildings?
questions.n: Because water is already in the pipes, activation is fast and there are fewer mechanical parts to fail.

questions.q: Which device sounds an alarm when there is a flow of water through the sprinkler system?
questions.n: This device detects movement in the pipes and sends a signal to the FACP.

questions.q: What is the term for a circuit that connects initiating devices (like smoke detectors) to the control panel?
questions.n: This circuit carries the input signals from sensors to the main panel.

questions.q: Which fire extinguisher type leaves no residue and is ideal for protecting sensitive electronics like servers?
questions.n: CO2 is a clean agent that displaces oxygen and cools the fire without leaving powders behind.

questions.q: In a dry pipe system, what is used to hold back the water at the main valve?
questions.n: The air pressure in the pipes keeps the dry pipe valve closed until a sprinkler head opens.

questions.q: What do you call a component that provides an audible or visible output, such as a horn or strobe?
questions.n: These devices 'notify' the occupants that there is an emergency.

questions.q: Which system is used in high-hazard areas where all sprinkler heads are open and the entire area is flooded simultaneously?
questions.n: Deluge systems provide a massive amount of water immediately to control rapidly spreading fires.

questions.q: Which fire extinguisher class is used for fires involving ordinary combustibles like wood, paper, and cloth?
questions.n: Class A is for 'Ash' producing materials like wood and fabric.

questions.q: What is the Fire Alarm Control Panel (FACP) often called in fire safety?
questions.n: It processes all input signals and coordinates all output notifications.

questions.q: Which extinguisher works by cooling the fire and removing the heat element of the fire tetrahedron?
questions.n: Water absorbs heat more effectively than most other common extinguishing agents.

questions.q: Where should fire extinguishers be located along a path of travel?
o: Along normal paths of travel and highly visible
Only in the basement near the utility room
questions.n: Visibility and ease of access are critical for emergency response times.

questions.q: What type of fire is a Class B extinguisher used for?
o: Fires involving flammable liquids and gases
questions.n: Class B is specifically for fuels like gasoline, oil, and grease.

questions.q: In a fire sprinkler system, what are 'risers'?
o: Vertical pipes that supply water to the sprinkler system
The valves that turn off the water
The specific heads that spray water
questions.n: Risers are the main vertical arteries of the plumbing network in a building.

questions.q: Which system requires BOTH a detection event and a sprinkler head opening to discharge water?
questions.n: This double-interlock feature is what makes pre-action systems safe for high-value rooms.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a Jockey Pump?
o: To cool the main fire pump
To maintain pressure in the sprinkler pipes
To pump water to the highest floor
questions.n: It keeps the system at a constant pressure so the main fire pump doesn't have to run for small leaks.

questions.q: Which type of standpipe system is intended for use by both firefighters and building occupants?
questions.n: Class III systems feature both 1.5-inch and 2.5-inch hose connections.

questions.q: What does the 'S' stand for in the P.A.S.S. acronym for fire extinguishers?
questions.n: The last two steps are to Squeeze the handle and Sweep the nozzle from side to side.

questions.q: Which of these is a Philippine-specific building law that focuses on accessibility?
questions.n: Batas Pambansa Bilang 344 is the law that enhances the mobility of disabled persons.

questions.q: What is the mandatory minimum height for a handrail above the floor or stair tread under BP 344?
questions.n: BP 344 specifies this range to accommodate people of various heights and disabilities.

questions.q: Which material is used in a fire extinguisher to interrupt the chemical chain reaction of a fire?
questions.n: Powders like Monoammonium Phosphate coat the fuel and break the chemical reaction.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the title of Section 13 of RA 9266?
questions.n: This section outlines the requirements one must meet to take the ALE.

questions.q: Which smoke detector is specifically designed to minimize false alarms from cooking steam?
questions.n: By sensing temperature instead of particles, it is immune to false alarms from steam or smoke.

questions.q: What is the maximum travel distance between fire extinguishers for a Class B hazard?
questions.n: Class B hazards require closer proximity because flammable liquid fires spread very fast.

questions.q: Which professional practice document in the Philippines was recently updated, as noted in current study reviews?
questions.n: New SPP documents have replaced the older versions to reflect modern architectural practice.
